note.explanation: Reactant molecules must collide with enough energy to form a transition state. The energy needed to reach this state is activation energy. A catalyst speeds up the reaction by providing a path with lower activation energy.
examples: In H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl, a collision with enough energy can form a transition state before HCl molecules form.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy, so more reactant molecules can form products.
note.checkAnswer: A catalyst increases the rate of reaction by lowering its activation energy.
note.simple: For a reaction to happen, molecules must collide with enough energy. A catalyst makes the reaction easier by lowering the energy needed.
note.checkQuestion: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
note.title: How reactions take place
steps: Reactant molecules move randomly and collide.
Only collisions with enough energy can form the transition state.
The transition state can return to reactants or form products.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy and increases the reaction rate.
note.answer: A catalyst increases the rate of reaction by lowering its activation energy.

mcqs.stem: Which statement best describes an effective collision?
rationales: This is wrong because many collisions do not produce a reaction.
This is right because enough energy is needed to form the transition state.
This is wrong because the molecules are in random motion before reacting.
This is wrong because collisions between reactant molecules are involved in forming products.

rationales: This is wrong because the text identifies molecules with more than average energy as excited.
This is wrong because average kinetic energy is not more than average.
This is right because the text calls molecules with more than average kinetic energy excited molecules.
This is wrong because the reactant molecules are described as being in random motion.

rationales: This is wrong because it describes released energy, not the energy needed to reach the transition state.
This is right because activation energy is the energy absorbed to convert molecules into the transition state.
This is wrong because the container walls do not define activation energy.
This is wrong because activation energy is an energy quantity, not a mass difference.

rationales: This is right because the catalyst changes the reaction path and substantially decreases activation energy.
This is wrong because a catalyst does not undergo permanent chemical change.
This is wrong because the catalyst decreases, rather than raises, the activation energy.

rationales: This is wrong because products at higher energy describe an endothermic profile.
This is wrong because equal reactant and product energy means no enthalpy difference.
This is right because the energy difference is given out as heat in an exothermic reaction.

The catalyst permanently becomes a product.
The catalyst makes all reactant molecules excited.
The catalyst removes the transition state from the reaction.
mcqs.stem: Which statement about the effect of a catalyst agrees with this section?
rationales: This is right because changing the reaction path lowers the activation energy.
This is wrong because a catalyst undergoes no permanent chemical change.
This is wrong because a catalyst does not make every reactant molecule excited.
This is wrong because a catalyst lowers the energy needed to reach the transition state rather than removing it.

written.text: Q6.2. Why is breaking of a bond an endothermic process?
written.finalAnswer: Energy must be absorbed to overcome the attraction holding the bonded atoms together.

rubric.why: Identifies that bond breaking requires an energy input.
rubric.description: State that energy is needed to break a bond.
rubric.how: Write that energy must be absorbed or supplied to break the bond.

rubric.why: Explains why the energy input is necessary.
rubric.description: Relate the energy input to overcoming the force holding the atoms together.
rubric.how: Explain that energy overcomes the attraction between the bonded atoms.

modelAnswer: Energy must be absorbed to overcome the attraction holding the bonded atoms together.
Therefore, breaking a bond is an endothermic process.

written.text: Q8.2. Explain why the reaction between atmospheric gases oxygen and nitrogen does not take place under normal conditions? But in the presence of lightning these gases react to give NO. The reaction stops as soon as the lightning stops.
written.finalAnswer: Under normal conditions, oxygen and nitrogen molecules do not have enough energy to overcome the activation energy and form the transition state. Lightning supplies the energy needed for the reaction to start. When lightning stops, that energy supply stops, so the reaction stops.

rubric.why: Explains why the gases do not react under ordinary conditions.
rubric.description: State that the molecules lack the energy needed for reaction.
rubric.how: Connect normal conditions with insufficient energy to overcome activation energy.

rubric.why: Identifies the energy source that allows the reaction to occur.
rubric.description: Explain that lightning supplies the needed energy.
rubric.how: State that lightning provides enough energy for the gases to react.

rubric.why: Links the energy supply to the reaction process.
rubric.description: Mention reaching the transition state or an effective collision.
rubric.how: Explain that the supplied energy allows molecules to reach the transition state.

rubric.why: Explains why the reaction stops when lightning ends.
rubric.description: State that the reaction stops when the energy source is removed.
rubric.how: Connect the end of lightning with the end of the energy supply and reaction.

modelAnswer: Under normal conditions, oxygen and nitrogen molecules do not have enough energy to overcome the activation energy and form the transition state.
Lightning supplies the energy needed for the reaction to start.
When lightning stops, that energy supply stops, so the reaction stops.
The reaction therefore produces NO only while the required energy is supplied.

written.text: Q8.3. A reaction between natural gas (CH₄) and atmospheric oxygen does not take place when you mix them. As soon as you show a burning match stick, the reaction starts immediately and then it continues until one or both of the reactants is/are used up. Explain.
written.finalAnswer: When CH₄ and oxygen are mixed, their molecules do not have enough energy to overcome the activation energy. The burning match supplies the energy needed to start the reaction by helping the molecules reach the transition state. The reaction then continues, releasing heat, until one or both reactants are used up.

rubric.why: Explains why mixing the gases alone does not start the reaction.
rubric.description: State that the mixed reactants lack the energy to begin reacting.
rubric.how: Refer to insufficient energy to overcome activation energy.

rubric.why: Identifies how the reaction is initiated.

rubric.why: Connects the supplied energy with the reaction pathway.
rubric.description: Mention reaching the transition state or producing effective collisions.
rubric.how: Explain that the energy helps reactant molecules reach the transition state.

rubric.why: Explains why the reaction continues after it starts.
rubric.description: State that it continues until reactants are used up.
rubric.how: Include the consumption of one or both reactants as the stopping condition.

modelAnswer: When CH₄ and oxygen are mixed, their molecules do not have enough energy to overcome the activation energy.
The burning match supplies the energy needed to start the reaction by helping the molecules reach the transition state.
The reaction then continues, releasing heat, until one or both reactants are used up.

written.text: Q8.1. Why is it essential to cook some of the food items while others we can eat without cooking?
written.finalAnswer: Cooking supplies energy to some food items and helps the chemical changes involved in cooking take place. Foods that can be eaten without cooking do not need this cooking process.

rubric.how: State that cooking provides heat or energy to the food.

rubric.description: Explain that cooking allows chemical changes to occur.
rubric.how: Mention the chemical changes or reactions involved in cooking.

rubric.why: Addresses why some foods are cooked.
rubric.description: State that some foods need the changes brought about by cooking.
rubric.how: Explain that some foods require cooking before they are eaten.

rubric.how: State that those foods do not need the cooking process.

modelAnswer: Cooking supplies energy to some food items and helps the chemical changes involved in cooking take place.
Some food items need these changes before they are eaten.
Other food items can be eaten without cooking because they do not need this cooking process.

examTips: Expect short questions asking for the meaning of activation energy, transition state, or catalyst.
For an explanation about a reaction starting with a flame or lightning, mention the energy supplied, activation energy, and the transition state.
Energy-profile questions may ask you to identify the transition state at the peak and activation energy between the reactant level and the peak.
For a catalyst question, state both that it lowers activation energy and that the catalyst does not undergo permanent chemical change.

steps.why: This is the hypothetical reaction given in your textbook.
The text explains that molecules move randomly and collide after the reactants are mixed.
steps.text: When A₂ and B₂ are mixed, their molecules collide with each other.

steps.why: A collision can form the transition state only when the molecules have enough energy.
steps.text: A collision between excited molecules may produce the transition state.

steps.why: The transition state can return to reactants or proceed to products.
steps.text: The transition state either returns to the reactants or forms the products, 2AB.

example.question: For the hypothetical reaction A₂ + B₂ → 2AB, describe how the reactants can form products.
example.answer: A₂ and B₂ molecules collide; a collision between excited molecules may form the transition state, which can then form 2AB.

explain.title: Molecules must collide
explain.body: A reaction takes place when the reactant molecules collide with each other to give a transition state. Molecules have different kinetic energies, so not every collision can produce a reaction.

explain.title: The transition state and activation energy
explain.body: The transition state is shown at the peak of the energy profile. The energy absorbed by the reactant or product molecules in order to be converted into the transition state is called the activation energy (Eₐ) of the reaction.

explain.title: Exothermic and endothermic profiles
explain.body: The difference between the energy of reactant and that of the product comes out in the form of heat representing enthalpy (ΔH) of the reaction. In an exothermic reaction, the products are at a lower energy than the reactants; in an endothermic reaction, they are at a higher energy.

explain.title: Catalysts
explain.body: A catalyst changes the path adopted by the reactants and substantially decreases the activation energy. More reactants can then be converted into product molecules, increasing the rate of reaction. A catalyst does not undergo permanent chemical change.

mistakes: Do not say that every collision produces products; molecules need enough energy to form the transition state.
Do not label the reactant energy level as the transition state; the transition state is at the peak of the profile.
Do not confuse activation energy with the enthalpy change between reactants and products.
Do not say a catalyst is permanently used up or becomes a product.
When explaining a reaction started by lightning or a flame, do not omit the energy needed to overcome activation energy.
